content: The map is clear. Let me confirm the abstraction definition in `internal/idp/idp.go`.

h03.
`internal/idp` (package `idp`); `internal/idp/oauth2` (package `oauth2`)

The abstraction lives in `internal/idp/idp.go`, which defines the provider-agnostic `IdentityProviderUserInfo` type (`internal/idp/idp.go:3`) — the common shape every provider maps a user into.

The single concrete protocol implementation is the OAuth2 integration in `internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go`, whose package comment states "Package oauth2 implements the OAuth2 identity provider integration" (`internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go:1`) and which provides `oauth2.IdentityProvider` and `oauth2.NewIdentityProvider` (`internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go:20,27`). It depends on `golang.org/x/oauth2` (`go.mod:37`). OAuth2 is the only shipped protocol — `internal/idp` contains no other implementation subpackage, and the provisioning docs confirm "Initial validation supports only OAuth2 providers" (`docs/configuration-provisioning.md:152`).
